title: Halve head dim: 4 heads -> 8 heads (HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64)
description: HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64, so model_dim stays 512 but n_head/n_kv_head go 4 -> 8; nothing else changed.
reflection: NEGATIVE, and cleanly so: val_bpb 1.000214 vs baseline 0.997358 (+0.0029 worse). The comparison was perfectly FLOP-matched as predicted -- 412.1M tokens, 3144 steps, 33.08% MFU, 50.3M params, all identical to baseline -- so this is a pure quality-per-FLOP readout with no throughput confound. Conclusion: at model_dim 512 with QK-norm and rotary, 4 heads of width 128 genuinely beat 8 heads of width 64. Head capacity matters more than head count here, which is the opposite of the GPT-2-era prior I argued from. The gradient on this axis points toward *wider* heads, not narrower, so HEAD_DIM 256 (2 heads) is the only remaining probe worth considering on it -- and 2 heads is probably too few to be a real candidate. I'd call the head-split axis settled at 128 and spend remaining runs elsewhere.
